title: Local module Hom is a sheaf
statement: Let (C,J) be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let R be a sheaf of rings, and let M,N be sheaves of R-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Define H(U) to consist of natural additive maps between the restrictions of M and N to C/U [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] that are linear over R(V) at every V over U, with restriction by precomposition on slices. Then H is a sheaf of sets, and H(U) is canonically equivalent to the set of R|U-linear morphisms M|U to N|U.

source.place: Tag 093T, proof of (1): the internal Hom sheaf; its local-linearity construction expanded using Mathlib Sites.SheafHom.

proof.text: Take Mathlib presheafHom of the underlying additive presheaves. Its section over U is an additive natural transformation on C/U. Impose sectionwise R-linearity, a predicate stable under all restriction maps. PresheafOfModules.homMk and forgetting linearity give inverse equivalences with module-sheaf maps on C/U. Restriction evaluation, composition, and identities agree by componentwise extensionality.

Mathlib Presheaf.IsSheaf.hom makes the ambient additive Hom presheaf a sheaf. Apply Subfunctor.isSheaf_iff. For a locally linear additive map, fix V over U, r in R(V), and x in M(V). The restrictions of the two sides of linearity to the pullback covering sieve agree by local linearity and naturality. Separatedness of N gives their equality over V, proving locality of the predicate and hence the sheaf condition.
